brief.headline: Microsoft is advertising 2,268 open roles across 56 countries. The largest single strategic cluster is Go-to-Market & Revenue (22.6% of postings), and 39.5% of all postings touch the AI / datacenter / silicon build-out.

sections.title: What the company is staffing for
points: The top three strategic clusters are Go-to-Market & Revenue (513), AI Platform & Copilot (394), Datacenter & Capacity Buildout (380).
1,037 roles (45.7%) build the product, 318 roles (14%) build physical capacity, 736 roles (32.5%) sell and serve, and 165 roles (7.3%) run the company.
The build-to-sell ratio is 1.41:1 — roughly balanced between creating capability and monetising it.
Security appears in 8.9% of postings, indicating it is treated as a cross-cutting requirement rather than a single team.

sections.title: Where the momentum is
points: 1,054 postings (46.5% of the open book) were created in the last 30 days.

Comparing the last three months of postings against the three before them, the clusters gaining share are Go-to-Market & Revenue (16.2% → 23.7%), Data & Analytics Platform (4.4% → 8%), Datacenter & Capacity Buildout (15.2% → 16.7%).

Over-represented in recent postings: Corporate & Enabling Functions (index 1.21), Go-to-Market & Revenue (index 1.18). An index above 1.0 means the theme takes a larger share of new postings than of the total.
Under-represented in recent postings: Quantum Computing (index 0.52), Silicon & Hardware Engineering (index 0.67), Azure Cloud Platform (index 0.73), Developer Tools & GitHub (index 0.75).
Geographies growing faster than their baseline: China (1.68), Netherlands (1.58), Canada (1.37), Ireland (1.3), United Kingdom (1.28).

sections.title: Which organisation is doing the hiring
points: Of the 55.7% of adverts that identify their own organisation, the split by division is Customer & Partner Solutions 25%, Engineering & product divisions 24.9%, Microsoft Frontier Company 5.8%.
The largest named units are Cloud Operations + Innovation (357), Solution Team Unit (148), Industry Solutions Delivery (108), Customer Success Unit (104), Account Team Unit (97).
Cloud Operations + Innovation (CO+I) alone accounts for 15.7% of the whole open book. Builds and runs the datacenter estate that all of Microsoft Cloud sits on.
Where a commercial solution area is named, the ranking is Security (172), Data & AI (141), Business Applications (124), Azure Infrastructure (55).
Growing faster than their own baseline: Account Team Unit (1.26×).

sections.title: The named bets
points: Agentic AI is referenced in 402 adverts (17.7%) — by a wide margin the most-cited initiative, and a sign that agents are being staffed as a product direction rather than a research topic.

The "Frontier" language splits in two. 36 adverts invoke the Frontier Firm transformation narrative — reorganising a company around AI agents — while 53 concern frontier-scale model training and the supercomputers behind it. The first is a go-to-market story sold to customers; the second is an engineering one.
Sovereign and regulated cloud appears in 52 adverts, indicating continuing demand from government and data-residency-constrained customers.

sections.title: How the organisation is being shaped
points: Leadership-titled postings (Manager through VP) account for 16.8% of the book; deep individual-contributor titles (Lead/Staff, Principal, Partner) account for 21%.
By declared role type the split is 90.6% individual contributor to 9.4% people manager — a flat structure, consistent with deepening existing teams rather than adding management layers.
Early-career and university postings are 2.9% of the book — a modest pipeline, with hiring concentrated on experienced staff.

sections.title: Location and working model
points: 52.5% of postings include a United States location. The next largest markets are India (228), Australia (100), Japan (94), United Kingdom (64).
605 postings (26.7%) list more than one location, indicating roles staffed opportunistically across sites.
Of postings that state a work-site policy, 80.2% require three or more days on-site and 12.3% are fully remote.

outlook: With 39.5% of hiring tied to AI, datacenter and silicon, the advertised plan is capital- and capability-led: Microsoft is staffing to expand the supply of AI compute, not just the demand for it.

The single largest named organisation is the datacenter arm (357 roles). When the biggest identifiable hiring block is the group that pours concrete and racks servers, the constraint being solved is physical capacity, not software headcount.

Agents are the through-line: 17.7% of all adverts mention agentic AI, spanning engineering, consulting and sales. That breadth suggests it is being treated as a company-wide operating assumption rather than one product team's bet.
Engineering is being added faster than field capacity, which usually precedes a product-expansion cycle rather than a revenue-harvest cycle.
The clearest forward signal among the strategic clusters is Corporate & Enabling Functions: it takes 1.21× its baseline share of the last 30 days of postings.
Geographic expansion is skewing toward China, Netherlands, Canada, suggesting capacity or market development outside the established hubs.
Since tracking began, the open book has moved +35 roles, with 659 postings opened and 643 closed — net expansion.
caveats: Based only on publicly advertised roles on careers.microsoft.com; internal transfers and unadvertised hiring are not visible.
A posting is not a hire — volumes indicate intent and capacity planning, not headcount actually added.

Business units are resolved from the posting’s structured department where that names the team outright, and otherwise from the way the advert describes itself in its Overview — never from the Responsibilities section, which names teams a role merely collaborates with. About two fifths of adverts resolve; the rest are reported as not stated rather than guessed, so unit totals are a floor, not a census.
The momentum index compares each theme’s share of the last 30 days of postings against its share of the whole open book. Roles that close quickly are slightly under-counted.
Cluster tagging is keyword-based over title, profession, discipline and description, after standard legal and benefits boilerplate is removed. Clusters overlap, so their shares do not sum to 100%.

The Frontier deep dive reads only the adverts that resolve to that organisation, which is a small cohort. Every figure there is therefore reported against the rest of the open book as an index rather than as a standalone number, and its recency window is 90 days rather than 30.

Requirements are read from each advert’s Qualifications block only, and the standard "languages including, but not limited to…" clause is counted as one open-list requirement rather than as demand for each language it names. The month-by-month market lines are survivorship-biased at their early end, since a role posted months ago is only visible if it is still unfilled — the demand index against the whole book is the sounder read.

reading: The Frontier organisation resolves on 131 adverts — 5.8% of the open book — split Industry Solutions Delivery 108, Frontier Company (unspecified unit) 18, Forward Deployed Engineering 5. A posting resolves either because its structured department names the team or because the advert describes itself as part of it, so this is a floor, not a census.
112 delivery-shaped roles in the cohort are matched by no classified selling role. This does not show whether existing staff or other teams generate demand.

The shape of the hire is Consultant (51, 55.57× the rest of the book), Architect (30, 5.33× the rest of the book), Program & project management (14, 1.84× the rest of the book). 17 postings carry a manager, director or VP title, which is management scaffolding rather than billable capacity.
67.2% of the cohort was created in the last 60 days, against 76.1% of the whole open book. Its hiring is no newer than the company’s as a whole.

13.7% of Frontier adverts commit to an industry vertical, against 12.1% in MCAPS and 2.1% in the engineering divisions. It is still a minority of the cohort, but it is several times the rest of the company, and it is the clearest evidence that this organisation is structured by market rather than by product. Where a vertical is named it is Financial Services (6), Defense & National Security (4), Government & Public Sector (3).

Direction of travel by vertical: Government & Public Sector takes 1.5× its baseline share of the cohort's last 30 days, while Defense & National Security takes 0.56×. On a cohort this size, read that as a lean, not a trend.
By role shape, People management (other) is over-represented in the last 30 days at 2.18× baseline — the clearest near-term signal of what the organisation thinks it is short of.

Against the other two divisions, Frontier is 64.1% consulting-shaped — architects, consultants and engagement leads — against MCAPS 13% and the engineering divisions 1.4%. It names an industry on 13.7% of adverts (MCAPS 12.1%, engineering 2.1%), and of the adverts that state a travel requirement, 19.1% ask for 25% or more (MCAPS 34.7%, engineering 5.7%).

The named capability stack is Azure (80), Copilot (44), Dynamics 365 (33), Azure AI Foundry (27). Agentic AI is cited on 35.9% of Frontier adverts against 6.7% in the engineering divisions — the delivery arm is talking about agents more than the people building them.

Geographically the cohort sits in 14 countries, led by India (42), United States (32), Japan (12), United Kingdom (8). The United States takes 24.4% of this cohort against 54.2% of the rest of the book — a markedly less US-weighted footprint, which is what a delivery organisation following customer demand looks like rather than one following the product groups.

The language that separates these adverts from the rest of the book is "elite engineers", "organization hosting", "delivery specialists", "existing intellectual" — phrasing about engagements and customer outcomes rather than about shipping product.

A further 46 adverts (2% of the book) name Frontier, ISD or FDE without claiming membership — roles told to work with the delivery arm rather than inside it. They cluster in Sales (30), Technology Sales (6), Business Operations (3), which is the surface area the organisation is being wired into.

strategy.title: ISD's future inside Frontier
strategy.scope: An evidence-led reading of possible strategic relevance, not a prediction that ISD will survive, shrink or be reorganised.
strategy.summary: The readable ISD adverts contain signals for make ai work in production; sell industry and business outcomes; scale beyond one-off engagements; connect delivery to lasting adoption; own complex, trusted implementation. These suggest possible ways for ISD to remain useful inside Frontier, not an approved survival strategy.
strategy.method: Only roles classified as ISD are evidence for ISD. FDE is a separate comparison, never folded into ISD. A signal requires a topic and an action in the same passage of Overview or Responsibilities; Qualifications are excluded. When only a published overview excerpt is available, coverage is limited. Counts are adverts, not independent decisions; shared wording is deduplicated in the source examples. These are heuristic text matches, not verified commitments.
strategy.frontierReading: The hypothesis to examine is complementary roles: ISD providing repeatable customer delivery and FDE providing forward-deployed engineering. The comparison below tests overlap in advertised work; it cannot establish a reporting line, a formal hand-off, budget allocation or replacement of one unit by the other.

signals.label: Make AI work in production
signals.inference: One possible role for ISD is turning AI ambition into implemented customer systems, rather than remaining a general-purpose consulting supplier.
signals.risk: AI vocabulary alone does not show production ownership, successful delivery or a profitable services model.
signals.watch: Look for explicit production accountability, operating metrics and customer references, not just more AI mentions.

evidence.title: Solution Architect
evidence.excerpt: Utilises a background in software product development or data platform implementation, as well as a strong understanding of current and emerging AI and machine learning services.

evidence.title: Solution Architect
evidence.excerpt: If you are excited by turning AI deployments into value that compounds cycle after cycle, this role is for you.

evidence.title: Senior Business Value Creation Lead
evidence.excerpt: In this role, you will own the Value Realization Framework end to end: surfacing where AI investment aligns with a customer's strategic objectives, building the value hypotheses and investment cases that unlock funding, declaring the measurement approach before anything is built, and proving realized outcomes against baselines once solutions are live.

signals.label: Sell industry and business outcomes
signals.inference: ISD could differentiate through customer context and measurable outcomes that a product team or generic implementation partner cannot supply alone.
signals.risk: Outcome-oriented language is not evidence that customers pay a premium or that ISD owns the commercial relationship.
signals.watch: Look for named industries, accountable outcome measures and ownership of complex engagements.

evidence.title: Solution Architect

evidence.title: ISD ASEAN Partner Commercial Lead

evidence.title: Solution Architect

signals.label: Scale beyond one-off engagements

signals.risk: A request to create accelerators does not establish asset reuse, better margins or a formal division of work with FDE.
signals.watch: Look for asset ownership, reuse targets, product feedback loops and named hand-offs between ISD and FDE.

evidence.title: Technology Consultant - CTJ - TS/SCI

signals.label: Connect delivery to lasting adoption

signals.risk: Adoption language does not prove incremental revenue or distinguish ISD ownership from CSU and partner responsibilities.

evidence.title: Technology Consultant - CTJ - TS/SCI

evidence.title: Regional Partner Commercial Leader - Industry Solutions Delivery (Americas)
evidence.excerpt: Work with deal teams to embed consumption-focused incentives and outcome-based elements into partner contracts, ensuring partners are motivated to deliver projects faster and drive Azure usage (e.g.

evidence.title: Consulting Project Manager - Oil, Gas, & Energy
evidence.excerpt: You will use industry benchmarks and tangible results desired to measure success as you drive value for customer through solution delivery while driving incremental cloud consumption and track key outcomes that drive cloud consumption and drive opportunity identification and delivers on the financial commitments of the Operation Model (Consumption Revenue, Industry Solutions Delivery (ISD) Direct Azure Impact, Delivery Value, Industry Solutions (IS) Billed Revenue), partnering with Area Consulting Leaders to establish controls to meet profit and loss (P&L) accountabilities.

signals.label: Own complex, trusted implementation
signals.inference: Complex integration and governance could be reasons to retain specialist ISD delivery capacity inside Frontier rather than relying only on standard product features.
signals.risk: Technical requirements do not establish exclusivity; partners and other Microsoft teams may offer the same capabilities.
signals.watch: Look for end-to-end accountability on difficult deployments and evidence of a distinct remit.

evidence.title: Consulting Project Manager - Oil, Gas, & Energy
evidence.excerpt: Identifies and implements the correct governance/delivery operating model and utilizes appropriate metrics for tracking customer satisfaction and puts feedback mechanisms in place in order to track solution success.

evidence.title: Senior Networking Project Manager - CTJ - TS/SCI
evidence.excerpt: Integrates security-first mindset into expectations for self and others.

evidence.title: Solution Architect
evidence.excerpt: Collaborates with the Project Manager to jointly drive project/technical governance of the design, build, and deployment, using enterprise architecture processes and ensuring quality control through peer review.

unknowns: Internal leadership intent, budgets, margins, utilisation and the approved organisation roadmap are not observable in job adverts.
Open postings are not headcount, completed hires or evidence of growth. A missing signal is not proof that a capability is absent.
ISD and FDE classification is heuristic. Compare the linked advert before relying on a unit assignment.
Repeated daily observations can track advertised requirements, but revenue, delivery success and organisational viability need independent evidence.

openList.label: Accepts any of several backgrounds
openList.note: "…or related roles" — an enumeration of acceptable histories

reading: 99.9% of the open book states its requirements, and those adverts name 3 distinct capabilities each. The capability the market is asked for most often is Delivery & programme (42% of adverts), ahead of Cloud & platform (32.3%).

By named skill the ranking is Delivery & programme management (22.6%), Azure (21.8%), Consulting & advisory (21.5%), Distributed systems (12.3%), Python (10.2%). Two clauses are deliberately kept out of that ranking because they enumerate options rather than state demands: 49.6% of adverts accept any of several backgrounds ("…or related roles") and 19.8% accept any mainstream language ("…languages including, but not limited to…"). Counted as skills they would be the two largest bars on the page while telling you nothing about what the job needs.

The median entry bar is 3 years of experience, and 86.4% of adverts name a degree. Across the bands the bar runs Intern / entry 1yr, Mid / unspecified 2yr, Senior 4yr, Principal + 5yr, Manager + 3yr — the manager band reads low because what it asks for is years of *people management*, a different clock from the technical bands.

The highest demand indices are Quota & pipeline (1.14×), Construction & commissioning (1.12×), PMP / delivery certification (1.11×), Industry domain knowledge (1.1×) — each takes that multiple of its baseline share in the last 90 days of postings.

The lowest are Azure certification (0.78×), Security clearance (0.78×), Azure AI Foundry / OpenAI (0.83×), Infrastructure as code (0.83×). On a book this size read those as a lean rather than a retreat.

The AI stack — LLMs, agents, retrieval and model operations — is named in 15% of the last 90 days of postings against 15.9% of the whole book, an index of 0.94. It is holding at its existing level rather than accelerating.

The entry bar moved -1 years across the plotted months (4 → 3 median). Earlier months are a survivorship-biased sample — only roles still open are visible — so read the recent end of that line, not its slope from the start.

The requirements that travel together most often are Azure + Consulting & advisory (225), Consulting & advisory + Customer-facing experience (136), AWS / GCP + Azure (126) — those pairs are the shape of the job the market is actually describing.
